request.query: Let A be a finite action set and Q(s,a) real valued. Adding a state-dependent action-independent constant c(s) to every Q(s,a) preserves argmax. Quantizing advantages Q(s,a)-max_b Q(s,b) so maxima remain zero and strict nonmaxima remain negative preserves a deterministic greedy policy.

theorems.name: Theorem 1 (Existence and uniqueness of optimal policy)
theorems.body: Under Assumption \ref {asm:frontdoor_crit}, (i) there exists an unique optimal deterministic stationary policy $\pi ^*$ whose $J(\pi ^*)$ is no worse than any other policies; (ii) $\pi ^*$ is greedy with respect to a weighted average of the $Q^{*}$. In particular, \begin {eqnarray}\label {eqn:optimalpolicy} \pi ^*(s)=\mathop{ {argmax}} _{a} \left [\sum _{\tilde {a},m} p_m(m|s,a) p_b(\tilde {a}|s)Q^*(s,\tilde {a},m)\right ]; \end {eqnarray} (iii) $Q^*$ satisfies the following Bellman optimality equation: \begin {eqnarray}\label {eqn:Belloptimal} Q^*(S_t,A_t,M_t)=\mathbb{E} \left [\left .R_t+\gamma \max _{a} \sum _{\tilde {a},m} p_m(m|S_{t+1},a) p_b(\tilde {a}|S_{t+1})Q^*(S_{t+1},\tilde {a},m)\right |S_t,A_t,M_t\right ]. \end {eqnarray}
theorems.slogan: An optimal deterministic stationary policy exists and is unique, performing at least as well as any other policy. This policy is greedy with respect to a weighted average of the optimal Q-values. The optimal action is chosen by maximizing a sum over mediator and baseline action probabilities. The optimal Q-function satisfies a Bellman equation involving expected rewards and future discounted values.

paper.title: Pessimistic Causal Reinforcement Learning with Mediators for Confounded Offline Data
